package.name: ai-efficiency-operating-system
package.purpose: Maximize useful AI progress per unit of context, tool use and iteration without sacrificing required capabilities, quality or verifiable completion.
package.source_coverage: current conversation plus existing cross-chat GitHub convergence artifacts and canonical repository skills
package.coverage_note: The current runtime did not return a complete account-wide chat corpus. Do not claim exhaustive account coverage. Existing pinned cross-chat GitHub artifacts are treated as the strongest available recovered history.

naming_policy.collision_rule: reuse_or_extend_canonical_semantics_before_creating_aliases; never overwrite a different semantic skill

review_topology.name: orchestrator
review_topology.duty: task ledger, root goal, dependencies, acceptance ownership

review_topology.name: cross-exam
review_topology.duty: challenge claims, provenance and naming collisions

review_topology.name: verifier
review_topology.duty: read-back, structural validation and acceptance evidence

review_topology.name: risk
review_topology.duty: rollback, overwrite, permission and compatibility risk

review_topology.name: adjudicator
review_topology.duty: retain best-supported solution and unresolved minority evidence

skills.name: root-goal-task-compiler
skills.description: Compile the request into a stable primary task, desired end state, negations, hard constraints, acceptance tests and evidence-backed root goal before substantive work.
conditions: newer explicit user correction overrides contradictory assumptions
supporting details do not silently replace the root goal
procedure: invalidate downstream assumptions when the user corrects direction
skills.example: For a repair request, preserve existing functionality and define success as target-runtime read-back rather than a plausible patch description.

skills.name: identity-and-path-lock
skills.description: Verify repository, branch or PR, file path, version, runtime/profile, owner/supersession relation and permissions before mutation.
conditions: do not guess a path from naming similarity
moving heads invalidate inherited exact-revision claims
skills.example: Before updating a skill, fetch the current file SHA on main and update that exact path rather than creating an almost-identical duplicate.

skills.name: evidence-gap-research
skills.description: Identify missing evidence before accepting important claims and prioritize sources or tests that can change the decision.
conditions: separate source classes
record contradiction instead of averaging it away
procedure: stop when marginal information gain collapses
skills.example: Do not assume a repository artifact is live product behavior; seek product guidance or runtime observation where the claim requires it.

skills.name: competing-hypotheses
skills.description: Keep multiple plausible explanations alive until discriminating evidence eliminates them.
conditions: minority hypotheses with stronger evidence survive majority disagreement
skills.example: For UI lag, distinguish context explosion, repeated tool discovery, serialization, retries and resource bottlenecks rather than blaming one visible symptom.

skills.name: root-cause-clustering
skills.description: Group symptoms by mechanism fingerprint and repair shared causes before symptom-by-symptom patches.
conditions: preserve required features
do not call removal or reduced usage a repair unless explicitly allowed
skills.example: If several chat surfaces slow together, inspect context routing, duplicate fetches and shared resource queues before separately tuning each screen.

skills.name: context-budget-routing
skills.description: Keep all capabilities available while loading only the context, tools and evidence needed for the current causal path.
conditions: do not disable useful tools globally
defer discovery until relevance is established
procedure: drop repeated paraphrase and stale branches
skills.example: Do not load every connector schema every turn; discover the GitHub write actions only when the task actually needs GitHub mutation.

skills.name: capability-challenge
skills.description: Distinguish visible, authorized and verified capability before claiming a tool can or cannot perform an action.
conditions: classify permission/auth/unsupported/infrastructure/unknown separately
procedure: attempt or read back capability where safe
skills.example: A visible GitHub connector is not proof of write permission; verify repo permissions or successful mutation.

skills.name: parallel-read-serial-write
skills.description: Parallelize independent investigation while serializing conflicting writes to mutable targets.
conditions: same-path writes require ownership and fresh SHA
dependent operations remain ordered
skills.example: Fetch several source files independently, but update the same catalog only after the package files are committed and the latest catalog SHA is known.

skills.name: multi-agent-deliberation
skills.description: Activate only roles that add distinct evidence, methods, capabilities, falsification pressure or verification duties.
conditions: role diversity is not runtime independence
scale by marginal information gain, not headcount
procedure: de-escalate when execution is more informative
record whether independence was observed or simulated
skills.example: Use source, root-cause, adversarial and verifier roles when each has a separate obligation; do not create ten approving clones.

skills.name: research-saturation-stop
skills.description: Stop gathering or debating when additional work no longer changes hypotheses, evidence confidence, risks or acceptance outcomes.
conditions: do not use fixed source count or elapsed time as depth metrics
skills.example: After multiple sources converge and only repeat the same claim, spend the next unit of effort on a runtime read-back instead.

skills.name: recoverable-state
skills.description: Persist task identity, checkpoints, evidence references, pending actions, irreversible actions and rollback targets so interruptions do not force full rework.
conditions: state must outlive transient model context when durability matters
procedure: rehydrate from evidence rather than memory
skills.example: A GitHub run should record the exact branch/head and unfinished verification gate so continuation resumes from evidence, not chat recollection.

skills.name: cross-chat-convergence
skills.description: Merge complementary cross-chat work by layer and exact source revision instead of copying summaries into competing skill names.
activation: multiple chats or PRs share one goal
conditions: deduplicate by semantic responsibility
source heads must be pinned or explicitly refreshed
procedure: retain one canonical owner per capability
skills.example: Keep archive recovery, portable reasoning skills and execution control plane as separate layers feeding one canonical skill system.

skills.name: runtime-performance-diagnosis
skills.description: Diagnose latency and stalls through context pollution, wrong routing, repeated work, cache misses, scheduling, retries, serialization and resource bottlenecks before reducing functionality.
conditions: preserve required feature set and quality
measure mechanism-specific signals
procedure: apply high-leverage fix and regression test
skills.example: Replace indiscriminate connector/schema loading with demand-driven discovery and cached stable metadata while leaving connectors available.

skills.name: completion-gate
skills.description: Prevent false completion by binding each acceptance criterion to evidence from the actual target revision/environment.
conditions: file existence or commit is not live verification
task failure and infrastructure failure remain distinct
procedure: state highest proven status and unresolved gaps
skills.example: After creating a skill file, fetch it from main and verify contents; still leave HOST_LIVE_VERIFIED open until the host actually loads it.

skills.name: high-density-finalization
skills.description: Perform necessary analysis and verification internally, then output only conclusions, decisive evidence, mechanisms, actions and material limitations.
conditions: compression must not hide unresolved acceptance gaps
do not use verbosity as proof of depth
skills.example: Report repository path, commit/read-back status, verified checks and the one unresolved account-history coverage limitation instead of dumping every intermediate step.

acceptance_tests: each skill has description, activation, conditions, procedure, example and provenance
canonical existing skills are composed rather than renamed into duplicates
runtime-independence claims require observed runtime receipts
repository commit claims require GitHub write receipt and read-back
host-live status remains unverified until actual host activation is observed
